Subject: Remote geo COLA proposal — EU & APAC adjustments for Q2 offers

Hi team,

I attached a first-pass COLA matrix for remote hires outside the US that PR/TA asked us to pilot for Q2 offers. The sheet has proposed percentage uplifts to base bands by city/market (zone-based — Core EU, Non-core EU, Singapore, India tiers). Key notes:

- Rationale: blend of local salary index + our cost-of-living rationale to keep offers competitive without breaking our US-centered banding.
- Proposed effective date: 2027-04-01 for new offers.
- Exceptions called out: Zurich + Singapore market premium (higher uplift but capped to a hard number to protect comp equity).
- Headcount impact: lifts estimated to increase offer-run-rate by ~2.1% for open reqs in the next 90 days.

Please review the attached "20270311-EU-APAC-COLA-matrix-draft.xlsx" and comment inline. Need decision on: (A) whether to adopt zone uplifts for all remote hires; (B) whether to allow hiring managers to approve up to 5% band exceptions locally; (C) confirm effective date.

Maya
People Ops (Rewards)
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Remote geo COLA proposal — benchmark report attached

Hi Maya / Laura / Marcus,

Thanks for sending the draft. Attached is a short benchmarking packet (see 20270311-TalentPartners-benchmarks.pdf) covering median market pay and 25/75 percentiles across the requested EU and APAC markets. Highlights:

- Zurich and London show the largest absolute gaps versus Redwood US mid-band; Zurich in particular justifies a premium >12% for senior ICs.
- Singapore shows similar percentile compression to London but local benefits costs are higher — recommend a fixed-market supplement vs % uplift to keep predictability.
- India (Bengaluru) and Poland remain highly cost-advantaged; small % uplifts (2–4%) keep offers competitive.

Recommended approach: use a hybrid — percent uplifts for non-peak markets, fixed supplement for Singapore/Zurich with manager approval required for amounts >$7,000 USD equivalent. We can provide a final vendor letter to attach to offer emails if you confirm.

Regards,
Valerie Hughes
Sr. Consultant, Talent Partners

Attachment: 20270311-TalentPartners-benchmarks.pdf (PDF, 12 pages)

Subject: Re: Remote geo COLA proposal — matrix + headcount note

Thanks, Valerie — helpful. Quick read-through and my asks before Rishi signs off:

- I like the hybrid approach. For market stability let's do fixed supplements for Singapore and Zurich (cap to $10k USD for senior ICs), percent uplifts for Core EU / Non-core EU / India tiers.
- For headcount discipline: hiring managers should be able to approve up to 3% band uplift locally for speed; anything above 3% (or any fixed supplement) requires Compensation approval.
- Need a one-page note for Finance that quantifies the incremental run-rate by headcount band (new hires only). Laura — can you produce that?

If ok with this, Rishi — can you confirm approval authority & effective date 2027-04-01?

Marcus Lin
VP, Talent Strategy
Redwood Inference

Subject: Final: Geo allowance approach & next steps

All — thanks for the quick turnaround. Per Rishi's sign-off: we will implement the hybrid approach with the following operational rules:

- Effective date: 2027-04-01 for new offers.
- Local manager uplift authority: up to 3% of mid-band. Anything above 3% or any fixed supplement requires Comp + Rishi sign-off.
- Fixed supplements: Singapore and Zurich only; capped at $10,000 USD, escalations >$7,500 to Rishi.
- Finance note: attached (candidate-offer-template-remote.pdf + cost run-rate sheet). Laura will share the one-page run-rate summary into the Drive linked below.

Neha — please coordinate with Talent Ops to add the vendor benchmark PDF to the offer email template and update the hiring manager FAQ.

I'll post the updated matrix in Drive by EOD.

Laura Bennett
